./docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-02-tsk-809-810-conversation-workbench-design.md:5:**Goal:** Bring the existing transcript-backed Claude and Codex conversation surface close to the Codex desktop experience while preserving MacCommandBar's session, workspace, tab, and PTY ownership model.
./docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-02-tsk-809-810-conversation-workbench-design.md:9:The existing Claude or Codex process remains authoritative. Conversation rendering reads its durable transcript and message submission writes to its existing PTY. The feature must never start a second provider process, attach another app-server or stream-json client, or infer state by scraping terminal pixels.
./docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-02-tsk-809-810-conversation-workbench-design.md:15:Use the Codex desktop app as the interaction and spacing reference while retaining MacCommandBar's Houston-derived color tokens. The conversation should feel quiet and readable rather than panel-heavy:
./docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-02-tsk-809-810-conversation-workbench-design.md:52:Rust scans only transcript locations already associated with the active parent session. Claude children are identified from sidechain/subagent metadata and Codex children from spawned-by/thread metadata. Each child record contains a stable child ID, parent ID, provider, label/role when available, lifecycle state derived from transcript evidence, timestamps, and a transcript locator.
./docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-02-tsk-809-810-conversation-workbench-design.md:72:- Rust fixture tests cover Claude parent/sidechain formats, Codex parent/spawned-thread formats, telemetry extraction, path validation, and attachment persistence.

./docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-04-assembly-acp-orchestration-and-orca-shell-amendment.md:10:This amendment was produced after re-reading the latest repository implementation and the two newest Superpowers plans, then comparing them with the clarified product requirements and the supplied Orca/Codex/ChatGPT screenshots.
./docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-04-assembly-acp-orchestration-and-orca-shell-amendment.md:40:No. An ACP session is a structured JSON-RPC connection between Assembly, acting as the ACP client, and an agent process or adapter, acting as the ACP agent. The client normally starts the adapter as a child process with piped stdin/stdout. That process is not an xterm instance and is not the native Claude Code or Codex TUI.
./docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-04-assembly-acp-orchestration-and-orca-shell-amendment.md:42:An ACP agent can report command/tool activity and may ask the client to provide terminal execution facilities. Those are **tool terminals** owned by Assembly and associated with a tool call. They may be shown as expandable command output or optionally opened in a terminal pane. They are not the same thing as the user-facing raw `claude` or `codex` TUI.
./docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-04-assembly-acp-orchestration-and-orca-shell-amendment.md:54:  Existing interactive PTY running the real Claude Code or Codex TUI.
./docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-04-assembly-acp-orchestration-and-orca-shell-amendment.md:59:### 1.2 Can ACP provide the requested Codex/T3-style controls and content?
./docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-04-assembly-acp-orchestration-and-orca-shell-amendment.md:63:For Codex and Claude, the reviewed official adapters already provide enough surface to build the requested product:
./docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-04-assembly-acp-orchestration-and-orca-shell-amendment.md:80:Yes. ACP is the default provider boundary, not a Codex/Claude-specific UI. Future providers enter through a curated `AgentProviderManifest` and the same `AgentRuntimeAdapter` contract. Provider differences remain in capabilities and namespaced metadata, while the visible timeline uses one app-owned canonical model.
./docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-04-assembly-acp-orchestration-and-orca-shell-amendment.md:93:- the Rust transcript scanners already discover Codex and Claude sessions, exclude helper/subagent sessions from the top-level rail, and derive titles, metadata, message counts, and resumable commands.
./docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-04-assembly-acp-orchestration-and-orca-shell-amendment.md:102:bare interactive `claude` or `codex` in a PTY
./docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-04-assembly-acp-orchestration-and-orca-shell-amendment.md:110:The repository also contains an intentionally unwired handwritten `codex app-server`/`claude -p stream-json` provider spike. It must not be independently activated beside the PTY. Its useful protocol discoveries can be preserved as tests or removed after the ACP runtime replaces it.
./docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-04-assembly-acp-orchestration-and-orca-shell-amendment.md:118:1. **New Codex and Claude sessions start structured by default through ACP.**
./docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-04-assembly-acp-orchestration-and-orca-shell-amendment.md:120:3. **The native CLI remains first class.** The user can hand a session to the raw Codex/Claude TUI and later return it to the structured view.
./docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-04-assembly-acp-orchestration-and-orca-shell-amendment.md:123:6. **`ownedId` remains the primary application identity.** ACP session IDs, Codex thread IDs, Claude session IDs, PTY IDs, tool-terminal IDs, workflow-run IDs, and parent/child IDs never replace it.

./docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-04-assembly-acp-orchestration-and-orca-shell-amendment.md:159:Do not invoke `npx ...@latest` per session. Pin the adapter version. ./docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-17-p3-conversation-live-workspaces.md:5:**Goal (user's #1):** Each Codex/Claude/CMUX conversation in the left rail becomes a **persistent, live workspace**. Clicking a conversation opens/restores its LIVE terminal (the conversation keeps running) plus its files / git / CWD / branch / worktree / browser. Switching to another conversation shows that conversation's live workspace while the previous one stays **ALIVE** (PTY never killed on switch). Unlimited live conversations, instant switch; an explicit **Close** tears exactly one down.

./docs/superpowers/evidence/tsk-808/a5-dispatch-spec-raw.log:753:No. An ACP session is a structured JSON-RPC connection between Assembly, acting as the ACP client, and an agent process or adapter, acting as the ACP agent. The client normally starts the adapter as a child process with piped stdin/stdout. That process is not an xterm instance and is not the native Claude Code or Codex TUI.
./docs/superpowers/evidence/tsk-808/a5-dispatch-spec-raw.log:755:An ACP agent can report command/tool activity and may ask the client to provide terminal execution facilities. Those are **tool terminals** owned by Assembly and associated with a tool call. They may be shown as expandable command output or optionally opened in a terminal pane. They are not the same thing as the user-facing raw `claude` or `codex` TUI.

    85	/** Normalize paths for identity without guessing anything about their content. */
    86	export function canonicalCwd(value: string | null | undefined): string {
    87	  const raw = (value ?? '').trim().replaceAll('\\', '/').replace(/\/+/g, '/');
    88	  if (!raw) return '';
    89	  if (raw === '/') return raw;
    90	  const withoutTrailingSlash = raw.replace(/\/$/, '');
    91	  // Preserve drive-letter paths while making their separator spelling stable.
    92	  if (/^[A-Z]:/.test(withoutTrailingSlash)) {
    93	    return `${withoutTrailingSlash[0].toLowerCase()}${withoutTrailingSlash.slice(1)}`;
    94	  }
    95	  return withoutTrailingSlash;
    96	}

   197	/**

   202	export function buildSessionLibrary(
   203	  owned: readonly OwnedSession[],
   204	  available: readonly AgentSession[]

   206	  const records: SessionLibraryRecord[] = [];
   207	  const ownedIds = new Set<string>();

   215	      provider: record.provider,
   216	      nativeSessionId: record.nativeSessionId,
   217	      cwd: record.canonicalCwd
   218	    });
   219	    if (identities.has(identity)) continue;
   220	    identities.add(identity);
   221	    records.push(record);

   227	    const identity = sessionIdentityKey({
   228	      provider: record.provider,
   229	      nativeSessionId: record.nativeSessionId,
   230	      cwd: record.canonicalCwd
   231	    });
   232	    if (identities.has(identity)) continue;
   233	    identities.add(identity);
   234	    records.push(record);
   235	  }
   236	  return records;
   237	}

   262	function dateInRange(value: string | null, from: string | null | undefined, to: string | null | undefined): boolean {
   263	  if (!from && !to) return true;
   264	  const stamp = value ? Date.parse(value) : Number.NaN;
   265	  if (!Number.isFinite(stamp)) return false;
   266	  if (from) {
   267	    const start = Date.parse(from);
   268	    if (Number.isFinite(start) && stamp < start) return false;
   269	  }
   270	  if (to) {
   271	    const end = Date.parse(to);
   272	    if (Number.isFinite(end) && stamp > end) return false;
   273	  }
   274	  return true;
   275	}

   278	  records: readonly SessionLibraryRecord[],

   320	export function paginateSessionLibrary(

   323	  pageSize = 50

    57	/**
    58	 * Runtime-only host lease for the one canonical workspace. It has no storage
    59	 * and no provider calls: the controller uses `move` when the same workspace
    60	 * changes center/right placement, so a second host cannot be mounted by
    61	 * accident while the first one is still live.
    62	 */
    63	export function createSessionLibraryMountCoordinator(): SessionLibraryMountCoordinator {
    64	  let current: { placement: SessionLibraryPlacement; active: boolean } | null = null;
    65	
    66	  const handleFor = (entry: { placement: SessionLibraryPlacement; active: boolean }): SessionLibraryMountHandle => ({
    67	    placement: entry.placement,
    68	    get active(): boolean {
    69	      return entry.active;
    70	    },
    71	    release(): void {
    72	      if (!entry.active) return;
    73	      entry.active = false;
    74	      if (current === entry) current = null;
    75	    }
    76	  });
    77	
    78	  const mount = (placement: SessionLibraryPlacement): SessionLibraryMountHandle => {
    79	    if (current) throw new Error(`Session Library already mounted in ${current.placement}`);
    80	    const entry = { placement, active: true };
    81	    current = entry;
    82	    return handleFor(entry);
    83	  };
    84	
    85	  return {
    86	    get mountedPlacement(): SessionLibraryPlacement | null {
    87	      return current?.placement ?? null;
    88	    },
    89	    mount,
    90	    move(placement): SessionLibraryMountHandle {
    91	      if (current) handleFor(current).release();
    92	      return mount(placement);
    93	    }
    94	  };
    95	}

    97	async function run(
    98	  handler: ((record: SessionLibraryRecord) => void | Promise<void>) | undefined,
    99	  record: SessionLibraryRecord
   100	): Promise<void> {
   101	  await handler?.(record);
   102	}

   104	/**
   105	 * Create the one action/refresh adapter shared by center and right placements.
   106	 * It deliberately captures callbacks, not session data; both placements can
   107	 * therefore reuse it without duplicating a scan or archive.
   108	 */
   109	export function createSessionLibraryService(
   110	  source: SessionLibrarySource = {},
   111	  handlers: SessionLibraryActionHandlers = {}
   112	): SessionLibraryService {
   113	  return {
   114	    async refresh(): Promise<SessionLibraryRecord[]> {
   115	      const owned = source.getOwnedSessions?.() ?? [];
   116	      const current = source.getAvailableSessions?.() ?? [];
   117	      const provider = source.listProviderSessions ? await source.listProviderSessions() : [];
   118	      return buildSessionLibrary(owned, [...current, ...provider]);
   119	    },
   120	    resume: (record) => run(handlers.onResume, record),
   121	    open: (record) => run(handlers.onOpen, record),
   122	    fork: (record) => run(handlers.onFork, record),
   123	    archive: (record) => run(handlers.onArchive, record),
   124	    delete: (record) => run(handlers.onDelete, record)
   125	  };
   126	}

   128	/** A no-op service is safe for a presentational host until the controller wires actions. */
   129	export const inertSessionLibraryService: SessionLibraryService = createSessionLibraryService();

   136	pub fn scan_sessions() -> Vec<AgentSessionRecord> {
   137	    let Some(home) = std::env::var_os("HOME").map(PathBuf::from) else {
   138	        return Vec::new();
   139	    };
   140	
   141	    let mut records = Vec::new();
   142	
   143	    // Sort the rollout files into "the user started this" and "Codex spawned
   144	    // this for itself" in one pass, keeping the ids of the second kind. Dropping
   145	    // sub-agent threads here, BEFORE the file budget, is for the same reason the
   146	    // Claude path drops its subagents first: they outnumber the user's own
   147	    // sessions nine to one, so a budget applied first would evict the sessions
   148	    // the rail exists to show.
   149	    let mut codex_files = Vec::new();
   150	    let mut codex_subagent_ids = HashSet::new();
   151	    for file in jsonl_files(&home.join(".codex/sessions")) {
   152	        match codex_rollout_thread_marker(&file) {
   153	            Some(marker) if marker.spawned_by_codex => codex_subagent_ids.extend(marker.id),
   154	            // No marker, or nothing readable: keep the file. Older Codex builds
   155	            // predate the field, and losing a session is the worse mistake.
   156	            _ => codex_files.push(file),
   157	        }
   158	    }
   159	
   160	    // Codex eventually moves a thread's rollout file into `archived_sessions`
   161	    // but leaves its index row behind, so for those threads the archive is the
   162	    // only evidence left of what kind of thread it was.
   163	    for file in jsonl_files(&home.join(".codex/archived_sessions")) {
   164	        if let Some(marker) = codex_rollout_thread_marker(&file) {
   165	            if marker.spawned_by_codex {
   166	                codex_subagent_ids.extend(marker.id);
   167	            }
   168	        }
   169	    }
   170	
   171	    let mut codex_records = Vec::new();
   172	    let codex_index = home.join(".codex/session_index.jsonl");
   173	    if let Ok(contents) = fs::read_to_string(codex_index) {
   174	        codex_records.extend(parse_codex_index_jsonl(&contents));
   175	    }
   176	    codex_records = drop_codex_subagent_sessions(codex_records, &codex_subagent_ids);
   177	
   178	    codex_files.sort_by(|a, b| modified_time(b).cmp(&modified_time(a)));
   179	    let mut codex_metadata = Vec::new();
   180	    for file in codex_files.into_iter().take(CODEX_SESSION_FILE_LIMIT) {
   181	        if let Ok(contents) =
   182	            read_head_and_tail_utf8(&file, CODEX_SESSION_HEAD_BYTES, CODEX_SESSION_TAIL_BYTES)
   183	        {
   184	            codex_metadata.extend(parse_codex_rollout_jsonl(&contents));
   185	        }
   186	    }
   187	    records.extend(merge_codex_session_metadata(codex_records, codex_metadata));
   188	
   189	    let cmux_term = home.join(".cmuxterm");
   190	    for (agent, file) in cmux_hook_session_files(&cmux_term) {
   191	        if let Ok(contents) = fs::read_to_string(file) {
   192	            records.extend(parse_cmux_hook_sessions_json(&agent, &contents));
   193	        }
   194	    }
   195	
   196	    let claude_projects = home.join(".claude/projects");
   197	    let mut files = jsonl_files(&claude_projects);
   198	    // Drop subagent transcripts and helper runs BEFORE the file budget is
   199	    // applied: they outnumber real sessions on a busy machine and would
   200	    // otherwise evict them.
   201	    files.retain(|file| !is_claude_subagent_transcript_path(file));
   202	    files.retain(|file| !claude_transcript_file_is_agent_launched(file));
   203	    files.sort_by(|a, b| modified_time(b).cmp(&modified_time(a)));
   204	    for file in files.into_iter().take(CLAUDE_SESSION_FILE_LIMIT) {
   205	        let project_path = file
   206	            .parent()
   207	            .and_then(|parent| parent.file_name())
   208	            .and_then(|name| name.to_str())
   209	            .and_then(decode_claude_project_dir)
   210	            .unwrap_or_default();
   211	        if let Ok(contents) = read_tail_utf8(&file, CLAUDE_SESSION_TAIL_BYTES) {
   212	            records.extend(parse_claude_jsonl(&contents, &project_path));
   213	        }
   214	    }
   215	
   216	    records = merge_agent_session_records(records);
   217	    records.sort_by(|a, b| b.last_activity.cmp(&a.last_activity));
   218	    records.truncate(AGENT_SESSION_RESULT_LIMIT);
   219	    with_derived_agent_session_metadata(records)
   220	}

   222	pub fn merge_agent_session_records(records: Vec<AgentSessionRecord>) -> Vec<AgentSessionRecord> {
   223	    let mut merged = Vec::<AgentSessionRecord>::new();
   224	
   225	    for record in records {
   226	        if let Some(existing) = merged
   227	            .iter_mut()
   228	            .find(|candidate| candidate.provider == record.provider && candidate.id == record.id)
   229	        {
   230	            merge_agent_session_record(existing, record);
   231	        } else {
   232	            merged.push(record);
   233	        }
   234	    }
   235	
   236	    merged
   237	}

   239	pub fn parse_codex_index_jsonl(input: &str) -> Vec<AgentSessionRecord> {
   240	    input
   241	        .lines()
   242	        .filter_map(|line| serde_json::from_str::<Value>(line).ok())
   243	        .filter_map(|value| {
   244	            let id = value.get("id")?.as_str()?.to_string();
   245	            let title = value
   246	                .get("thread_name")
   247	                .and_then(Value::as_str)
   248	                .unwrap_or(CODEX_UNTITLED_INDEX_TITLE)
   249	                .to_string();
   250	            let last_activity = value
   251	                .get("updated_at")
   252	                .and_then(Value::as_str)
   253	                .map(ToOwned::to_owned);
   254	
   255	            Some(AgentSessionRecord {
   256	                provider: "codex".to_string(),
   257	                id: id.clone(),
   258	                title,
   259	                description: None,
   260	                model: model_from_value(&value),
   261	                project_path: None,
   262	                last_activity,
   263	                resume_commands: vec![format!("codex resume {id}")],
   264	                branch_hint: None,
   265	                task_id: None,
   266	                pull_request_hint: None,
   267	                source_label: None,
   268	                message_count: None,
   269	                latest_turn_preview: None,
   270	            })
   271	        })
   272	        .collect()
   273	}
   274	
   275	pub fn parse_codex_rollout_jsonl(input: &str) -> Vec<AgentSessionRecord> {
   276	    let mut records: Vec<AgentSessionRecord> = Vec::new();
   277	    let mut first_prompts: HashMap<String, String> = HashMap::new();
   278	    let mut message_counts: HashMap<String, u32> = HashMap::new();
   279	    let mut latest_turns: HashMap<String, String> = HashMap::new();
   280	    // Who spoke last in each session, so a run of agent narration can be
   281	    // counted as the one thing the agent said rather than as twenty.
   282	    let mut last_speakers: HashMap<String, CodexSpeaker> = HashMap::new();
   283	
   284	    for value in input
   285	        .lines()
   286	        .filter_map(|line| serde_json::from_str::<Value>(line).ok())
   287	    {
   288	        match value.get("type").and_then(Value::as_str) {
   289	            Some("session_meta") => {
   290	                let Some(payload) = value.get("payload") else {
   291	                    continue;
   292	                };
   293	                if is_codex_subagent_meta(payload) {
   294	                    return Vec::new();
   295	                }
   296	                let Some(id) = payload.get("id").and_then(Value::as_str) else {
   297	                    continue;
   298	                };
   299	
   300	                let cwd = payload
   301	                    .get("cwd")
   302	                    .and_then(Value::as_str)
   303	                    .filter(|value| !value.trim().is_empty())
   304	                    .map(ToOwned::to_owned);
   305	                let last_activity = value
   306	                    .get("timestamp")
   307	                    .and_then(Value::as_str)
   308	                    .or_else(|| payload.get("timestamp").and_then(Value::as_str))
   309	                    .map(ToOwned::to_owned);
   310	
   311	                let record = AgentSessionRecord {
   312	                    provider: "codex".to_string(),
   313	                    id: id.to_string(),
   314	                    title: CODEX_GENERIC_SESSION_TITLE.to_string(),
   315	                    description: None,
   316	                    model: model_from_value(payload),
   317	                    project_path: cwd,
   318	                    last_activity,
   319	                    resume_commands: vec![format!("codex resume {id}")],
   320	                    branch_hint: None,
   321	                    task_id: None,
   322	                    pull_request_hint: None,
   323	                    source_label: None,
   324	                    message_count: None,
   325	                    latest_turn_preview: None,
   326	                };
   327	
   328	                if let Some(existing) = records.iter_mut().find(|candidate| {
   329	                    candidate.provider == record.provider && candidate.id == record.id
   330	                }) {
   331	                    merge_codex_record(existing, record);
   332	                } else {
   333	                    records.push(record);
   334	                }
   335	            }
   336	            Some("turn_context") => {
   337	                let Some(payload) = value.get("payload") else {
   338	                    continue;
   339	                };
   340	
   341	                let cwd = payload
   342	                    .get("cwd")
   343	                    .and_then(Value::as_str)
   344	                    .filter(|value| !value.trim().is_empty())
   345	                    .map(ToOwned::to_owned);
   346	                let last_activity = value
   347	                    .get("timestamp")
   348	                    .and_then(Value::as_str)
   349	                    .map(ToOwned::to_owned);
   350	                update_latest_codex_record(
   351	                    &mut records,
   352	                    cwd,
   353	                    None,
   354	                    model_from_value(payload),
   355	                    last_activity,
   356	                );
   357	            }
   358	            Some("response_item") => {
   359	                if let (Some(record), Some(prompt)) =
   360	                    (records.last(), codex_user_prompt_text(&value))
   361	                {
   362	                    first_prompts.entry(record.id.clone()).or_insert(prompt);
   363	                }
   364	
   365	                if let Some(id) = records.last().map(|record| record.id.clone()) {
   366	                    if let Some((speaker, turn)) = codex_conversation_turn(&value) {
   367	                        // Codex writes a separate record for every paragraph it
   368	                        // narrates between tool calls, so a run of them is ONE
   369	                        // thing the agent said back, not twenty. Without this a
   370	                        // Codex row read "691 messages" where the Claude row
   371	                        // beside it, for a longer conversation, read "33".
   372	                        let repeat_narration = speaker == CodexSpeaker::Agent
   373	                            && last_speakers.get(&id) == Some(&CodexSpeaker::Agent);
   374	                        if !repeat_narration {
   375	                            *message_counts.entry(id.clone()).or_insert(0) += 1;
   376	                        }
   377	                        last_speakers.insert(id.clone(), speaker);
   378	                        latest_turns.insert(id, turn); // a later line is the newer turn
   379	                    }
   380	                }
   381	
   382	                let cwd = codex_response_item_workdir(&value);
   383	                let description = codex_response_item_description(&value);
   384	                if cwd.is_none() && description.is_none() {
   385	                    continue;
   386	                };
   387	                let last_activity = value
   388	                    .get("timestamp")
   389	                    .and_then(Value::as_str)
   390	                    .map(ToOwned::to_owned);
   391	                update_latest_codex_record(&mut records, cwd, description, None, last_activity);
   392	            }
   393	            _ => {}
   394	        }
   395	    }
   396	
   397	    for record in records.iter_mut() {
   398	        record.title = codex_display_title(
   399	            &record.title,
   400	            first_prompts.get(&record.id).map(String::as_str),
   401	        );
   402	        record.message_count = message_counts.get(&record.id).copied();
   403	        record.latest_turn_preview = latest_turns.get(&record.id).cloned();
   404	    }
   405	
   406	    records
   407	}
   408	
   409	/// Who said one message of a Codex conversation.
   410	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
   411	enum CodexSpeaker {
   412	    User,
   413	    Agent,
   414	}
   415	
   416	/// One message of a Codex conversation: who said it, and how a row would show
   417	/// it. The user side uses the same filter the title does, so the opening turns
   418	/// Codex writes for itself — the repository instructions, the environment block
   419	/// — are neither counted nor shown; the agent side needs actual words.
   420	fn codex_conversation_turn(value: &Value) -> Option<(CodexSpeaker, String)> {
   421	    let payload = value.get("payload")?;
   422	    if payload.get("type").and_then(Value::as_str) != Some("message") {
   423	        return None;
   424	    }
   425	
   426	    match payload.get("role").and_then(Value::as_str)? {
   427	        "user" => Some((
   428	            CodexSpeaker::User,
   429	            agent_session_turn_preview(
   430	                AGENT_SESSION_USER_TURN_PREFIX,
   431	                &codex_typed_user_text(value)?,
   432	            ),
   433	        )),
   434	        "assistant" => {
   435	            let text = payload.get("content").and_then(value_to_text)?;
   436	            let text = text.trim();
   437	            (!text.is_empty()).then(|| {
   438	                (
   439	                    CodexSpeaker::Agent,
   440	                    agent_session_turn_preview(AGENT_SESSION_AGENT_TURN_PREFIX, text),
   441	                )
   442	            })
   443	        }
   444	        _ => None,
   445	    }
   446	}
   447	
   448	/// Codex spawns its own helper threads and writes each one as a rollout file
   449	/// next to the user's, so nine of every ten files under `~/.codex/sessions` are
   450	/// threads nobody opened. The opening `session_meta` record says which it is:
   451	/// a helper carries `thread_source: "subagent"`, and/or a `source` object whose
   452	/// only key is `subagent` (a session the user started has `source` as a plain
   453	/// string — `cli`, `vscode`, `exec`).
   454	///
   455	/// Verified 2026-07-28 across 687 rollout files on this machine: 619 helper
   456	/// threads, 68 sessions the user started, and the two markers disagreed on a
   457	/// single file — so both are checked and either one is enough.
   458	///
   459	/// A file with neither marker is kept. Older Codex versions predate the field
   460	/// (15 files here), and losing one of the user's sessions is worse than listing
   461	/// a helper thread.
   462	fn is_codex_subagent_meta(payload: &Value) -> bool {
   463	    if payload.get("thread_source").and_then(Value::as_str) == Some("subagent") {
   464	        return true;
   465	    }
   466	
   467	    payload
   468	        .get("source")
   469	        .and_then(Value::as_object)
   470	        .is_some_and(|source| source.contains_key("subagent"))
   471	}
   472	
   473	/// What a rollout file's opening metadata record says about its thread. The id
   474	/// can be missing while the verdict is still known, so the two are separate.
   475	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
   476	pub struct CodexThreadMarker {
   477	    pub id: Option<String>,
   478	    pub spawned_by_codex: bool,
   479	}
   480	
   481	/// Read from a bounded head, so the scan can sort the files before it spends
   482	/// its read budget on them.
   483	fn codex_rollout_thread_marker(path: &Path) -> Option<CodexThreadMarker> {
   484	    let head = read_head_utf8(path, CODEX_SESSION_META_PROBE_BYTES).ok()?;
   485	    codex_rollout_head_thread_marker(&head)
   486	}
   487	
   488	/// `None` when the head holds no readable metadata record — a truncated line, a
   489	/// file that opens with something else, an empty file. The caller keeps those.
   490	pub fn codex_rollout_head_thread_marker(head: &str) -> Option<CodexThreadMarker> {
   491	    let line = head.lines().next()?;
   492	    let value = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(line).ok()?;
   493	    if value.get("type").and_then(Value::as_str) != Some("session_meta") {
   494	        return None;
   495	    }
   496	
   497	    let payload = value.get("payload")?;
   498	    Some(CodexThreadMarker {
   499	        id: payload
   500	            .get("id")
   501	            .and_then(Value::as_str)
   502	            .map(ToOwned::to_owned),
   503	        spawned_by_codex: is_codex_subagent_meta(payload),
   504	    })
   505	}
   506	
   507	pub fn codex_rollout_head_is_subagent_thread(head: &str) -> bool {
   508	    codex_rollout_head_thread_marker(head).is_some_and(|marker| marker.spawned_by_codex)
   509	}
   510	
   511	/// Index rows naming threads Codex spawned for itself.
   512	///
   513	/// `~/.codex/session_index.jsonl` is a flat list of id, name and timestamp with
   514	/// nothing in it saying what kind of thread a row describes, so the rollout
   515	/// files are the only evidence — and the index is read whole, with none of the
   516	/// filtering the rollout files get. On this machine 119 of its 330 rows are
   517	/// sub-agent threads, 117 of them already archived, and every one of those was
   518	/// reaching the rail under a plausible name ("Audit inventory gaps", "Review
   519	/// mobile steppers") that gave the user no way to tell it apart from their own
   520	/// work.
   521	///
   522	/// A row whose thread has no rollout file left anywhere is kept: 150 of them
   523	/// here, all genuinely the user's, and absence of evidence is not evidence.
   524	pub fn drop_codex_subagent_sessions(
   525	    records: Vec<AgentSessionRecord>,
   526	    subagent_ids: &HashSet<String>,
   527	) -> Vec<AgentSessionRecord> {
   528	    records
   529	        .into_iter()
   530	        .filter(|record| !subagent_ids.contains(&record.id))
   531	        .collect()
   532	}
   533	
   534	/// The first thing the user actually typed. Codex opens every session with
   535	/// machine-written turns sent as the user — the repository's `AGENTS.md`, the
   536	/// environment block, the plugin list, the file list — and each has a shape we
   537	/// can recognise, so the title comes from the first turn that is none of them.
   538	fn codex_user_prompt_text(value: &Value) -> Option<String> {
   539	    codex_typed_user_text(value).map(|text| compact_text(&text, 140))
   540	}
   541	
   542	/// The same turn, at full length, for callers that do their own cutting.
   543	fn codex_typed_user_text(value: &Value) -> Option<String> {
   544	    let payload = value.get("payload")?;
   545	    if payload.get("type").and_then(Value::as_str) != Some("message") {
   546	        return None;
   547	    }
   548	    if payload.get("role").and_then(Value::as_str) != Some("user") {
   549	        return None;
   550	    }
   551	
   552	    let text = payload.get("content").and_then(value_to_text)?;
   553	    let text = text.trim();
   554	    if text.is_empty() || CODEX_INJECTED_PROMPT_PREFIXES.iter().any(|prefix| text.starts_with(prefix)) {
   555	        return None;
   556	    }
   557	
   558	    Some(text.to_string())
   559	}
   560	
   561	/// Openings that mean Codex wrote this turn, not the user. `<` covers every
   562	/// tagged block it injects (`<environment_context>`, `<recommended_plugins>`,
   563	/// `<user_shell_command>`); the two headings are the repository instructions
   564	/// and the attached-file list.
   565	const CODEX_INJECTED_PROMPT_PREFIXES: &[&str] = &[
   566	    "<",
   567	    "# AGENTS.md instructions",
   568	    "# Files mentioned by the user",
   569	];
   570	
   571	/// A Codex rollout file carries no title of its own, so a rail built from these
   572	/// files alone reads as hundreds of rows all saying "Codex session". The first
   573	/// typed prompt is the only description of the session in the file, so it
   574	/// becomes the title; the generic label survives only when the scanned window
   575	/// held no typed prompt at all.
   576	fn codex_display_title(derived: &str, first_prompt: Option<&str>) -> String {
   577	    if derived != CODEX_GENERIC_SESSION_TITLE {
   578	        return derived.to_string();
   579	    }
   580	
   581	    match first_prompt {
   582	        Some(prompt) => compact_text(prompt, 60),
   583	        None => CODEX_GENERIC_SESSION_TITLE.to_string(),
   584	    }
   585	}
   586	
   587	fn is_generic_codex_title(title: &str) -> bool {
   588	    title == CODEX_GENERIC_SESSION_TITLE || title == CODEX_UNTITLED_INDEX_TITLE
   589	}
   590	
   591	/// One Codex session can be described twice: the index file may name it, and
   592	/// the rollout file offers the opening prompt. Whichever record looks newer is
   593	/// beside the point — a placeholder must never displace a real title, and the
   594	/// index name describes the whole session where the prompt only opens it, so
   595	/// the title already in hand wins when both are real.
   596	fn better_codex_title(existing: String, candidate: String) -> String {
   597	    if !is_generic_codex_title(&existing) {
   598	        return existing;
   599	    }
   600	    if !is_generic_codex_title(&candidate) {
   601	        return candidate;
   602	    }
   603	
   604	    existing
   605	}
   606	
   607	fn update_latest_codex_record(
   608	    records: &mut [AgentSessionRecord],
   609	    cwd: Option<String>,
   610	    description: Option<String>,
   611	    model: Option<String>,
   612	    last_activity: Option<String>,
   613	) {
   614	    let Some(record) = records.last_mut() else {
   615	        return;
   616	    };
   617	
   618	    let id = record.id.clone();
   619	    let update = AgentSessionRecord {
   620	        provider: "codex".to_string(),
   621	        id: id.clone(),
   622	        title: record.title.clone(),
   623	        description,
   624	        model,
   625	        project_path: cwd,
   626	        last_activity,
   627	        resume_commands: vec![format!("codex resume {id}")],
   628	        branch_hint: None,
   629	        task_id: None,
   630	        pull_request_hint: None,
   631	        source_label: None,
   632	        message_count: None,
   633	        latest_turn_preview: None,
   634	    };
   635	    merge_codex_record(record, update);
   636	}
   637	
   638	fn codex_response_item_workdir(value: &Value) -> Option<String> {
   639	    let payload = value.get("payload")?;
   640	    if payload.get("type").and_then(Value::as_str) != Some("function_call") {
   641	        return None;
   642	    }
   643	
   644	    let arguments = payload.get("arguments").and_then(Value::as_str)?;
   645	    let arguments = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(arguments).ok()?;
   646	    optional_string(arguments.get("workdir"))
   647	}
   648	
   649	fn codex_response_item_description(value: &Value) -> Option<String> {
   650	    let payload = value.get("payload")?;
   651	    if payload.get("type").and_then(Value::as_str) != Some("message") {
   652	        return None;
   653	    }
   654	    if payload.get("role").and_then(Value::as_str) != Some("user") {
   655	        return None;
   656	    }
   657	
   658	    payload
   659	        .get("content")
   660	        .and_then(value_to_text)
   661	        .map(|text| compact_text(&text, 140))
   662	}
   663	
   664	pub fn merge_codex_session_metadata(
   665	    mut indexed: Vec<AgentSessionRecord>,
   666	    metadata: Vec<AgentSessionRecord>,
   667	) -> Vec<AgentSessionRecord> {
   668	    for record in metadata {
   669	        if let Some(existing) = indexed
   670	            .iter_mut()
   671	            .find(|candidate| candidate.provider == record.provider && candidate.id == record.id)
   672	        {
   673	            merge_codex_record(existing, record);
   674	        } else {
   675	            indexed.push(record);
   676	        }
   677	    }
   678	
   679	    indexed
   680	}
   681	
   682	pub fn parse_cmux_hook_sessions_json(agent: &str, input: &str) -> Vec<AgentSessionRecord> {
   683	    let Ok(value) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(input) else {
   684	        return Vec::new();
   685	    };
   686	    let Some(sessions) = value.get("sessions").and_then(Value::as_object) else {
   687	        return Vec::new();
   688	    };
   689	
   690	    let agent = agent.trim().to_lowercase();
   691	    if agent.is_empty() {
   692	        return Vec::new();
   693	    }
   694	
   695	    sessions
   696	        .iter()
   697	        .filter_map(|(key, value)| {
   698	            let id = value
   699	                .get("sessionId")
   700	                .and_then(Value::as_str)
   701	                .unwrap_or(key)
   702	                .trim();
   703	            if id.is_empty() {
   704	                return None;
   705	            }
   706	
   707	            let cwd = value
   708	                .get("cwd")
   709	                .and_then(Value::as_str)
   710	                .or_else(|| {
   711	                    value
   712	                        .get("launchCommand")
   713	                        .and_then(|launch| launch.get("workingDirectory"))
   714	                        .and_then(Value::as_str)
   715	                })
   716	                .filter(|value| !value.trim().is_empty())
   717	                .map(ToOwned::to_owned);
   718	            let last_activity = timestampish_string(value.get("updatedAt"))
   719	                .or_else(|| timestampish_string(value.get("startedAt")))
   720	                .or_else(|| {
   721	                    timestampish_string(
   722	                        value
   723	                            .get("launchCommand")
   724	                            .and_then(|launch| launch.get("capturedAt")),
   725	                    )
   726	                });
   727	            let status = value
   728	                .get("runtimeStatus")
   729	                .and_then(Value::as_str)
   730	                .or_else(|| value.get("agentLifecycle").and_then(Value::as_str))
   731	                .filter(|value| !value.trim().is_empty());
   732	            let title = cmux_session_title(&agent, value, status, cwd.as_deref());
   733	
   734	            Some(AgentSessionRecord {
   735	                provider: format!("cmux-{agent}"),
   736	                id: id.to_string(),
   737	                title,
   738	                description: cmux_session_description(value),
   739	                model: model_from_value(value),
   740	                project_path: cwd.clone(),
   741	                last_activity,
   742	                resume_commands: cmux_resume_commands(&agent, id, cwd.as_deref()),
   743	                branch_hint: None,
   744	                task_id: None,
   745	                pull_request_hint: None,
   746	                source_label: None,
   747	                message_count: None,
   748	                latest_turn_preview: None,
   749	            })
   750	        })
   751	        .collect()
   752	}
   753	
   754	pub fn parse_claude_jsonl(input: &str, project_path: &str) -> Vec<AgentSessionRecord> {
   755	    let mut records: Vec<AgentSessionRecord> = Vec::new();
   756	    let mut ai_titles: HashMap<String, String> = HashMap::new();
   757	    let mut first_prompts: HashMap<String, String> = HashMap::new();
   758	    let mut message_counts: HashMap<String, u32> = HashMap::new();
   759	    let mut latest_turns: HashMap<String, String> = HashMap::new();
   760	
   761	    for value in input
   762	        .lines()
   763	        .filter_map(|line| serde_json::from_str::<Value>(line).ok())
   764	    {
   765	        // One such entry condemns the whole transcript: these files are what
   766	        // they are end to end, so anything already collected from one is an
   767	        // agent's turn, not a session the user can resume. Both checks answer
   768	        // the same question — "is this a top-level session?" — from different
   769	        // evidence: a subagent's sidechain flag, or a helper's entrypoint.
   770	        if is_claude_sidechain_entry(&value) || is_claude_agent_launched_entry(&value) {
   771	            return Vec::new();
   772	        }
   773	
   774	        if let Some((session, title)) = claude_ai_title(&value) {
   775	            ai_titles.insert(session, title); // a later line carries the newer title
   776	        }
   777	        if let Some((session, prompt)) = claude_user_prompt_text(&value) {
   778	            first_prompts.entry(session).or_insert(prompt);
   779	        }
   780	        if let Some((session, turn)) = claude_conversation_turn(&value) {
   781	            *message_counts.entry(session.clone()).or_insert(0) += 1;
   782	            latest_turns.insert(session, turn); // a later line is the newer turn
   783	        }
   784	
   785	        let Some(id) = value
   786	            .get("sessionId")
   787	            .or_else(|| value.get("session_id"))
   788	            .and_then(Value::as_str)
   789	        else {
   790	            continue;
   791	        };
   792	
   793	        let timestamp = value
   794	            .get("timestamp")
   795	            .or_else(|| value.get("created_at"))
   796	            .and_then(Value::as_str)
   797	            .map(ToOwned::to_owned);
   798	
   799	        let cwd = value
   800	            .get("cwd")
   801	            .and_then(Value::as_str)
   802	            .unwrap_or(project_path)
   803	            .to_string();
   804	
   805	        let title = title_from_claude_message(&value)
   806	            .unwrap_or_else(|| CLAUDE_GENERIC_SESSION_TITLE.to_string());
   807	        let record = AgentSessionRecord {
   808	            provider: "claude".to_string(),
   809	            id: id.to_string(),
   810	            title,
   811	            description: claude_session_description(&value),
   812	            model: value
   813	                .get("message")
   814	                .and_then(model_from_value)
   815	                .or_else(|| model_from_value(&value)),
   816	            project_path: (!cwd.is_empty()).then_some(cwd.clone()),
   817	            last_activity: timestamp,
   818	            resume_commands: vec![
   819	                format!("claude --resume {id}"),
   820	                format!("cd {} && claude --resume {id}", shell_quote(&cwd)),
   821	            ],
   822	            branch_hint: None,
   823	            task_id: None,
   824	            pull_request_hint: None,
   825	            source_label: None,
   826	            message_count: None,
   827	            latest_turn_preview: None,
   828	        };
   829	
   830	        if let Some(existing) = records
   831	            .iter_mut()
   832	            .find(|candidate| candidate.provider == record.provider && candidate.id == record.id)
   833	        {
   834	            merge_agent_session_record(existing, record);
   835	        } else {
   836	            records.push(record);
   837	        }
   838	    }
   839	
   840	    for record in records.iter_mut() {
   841	        record.title = claude_display_title(
   842	            &record.title,
   843	            ai_titles.get(&record.id).map(String::as_str),
   844	            first_prompts.get(&record.id).map(String::as_str),
   845	            record.project_path.as_deref(),
   846	        );
   847	        record.message_count = message_counts.get(&record.id).copied();
   848	        record.latest_turn_preview = latest_turns.get(&record.id).cloned();
   849	    }
   850	
   851	    records
   852	}
   853	
   854	/// One turn of the conversation as a row counts it, and how that row would show
   855	/// it. Tool calls and tool results are `type: "user"` and `type: "assistant"`
   856	/// records too, so both sides insist on actual words: a user turn goes through
   857	/// the same filter the title uses (no slash-command wrappers, no resume
   858	/// caveat), and an assistant turn needs at least one text block.
   859	fn claude_conversation_turn(value: &Value) -> Option<(String, String)> {
   860	    match optional_string(value.get("type"))?.as_str() {
   861	        "user" => {
   862	            let (id, text) = claude_user_prompt_text(value)?;
   863	            Some((
   864	                id,
   865	                agent_session_turn_preview(AGENT_SESSION_USER_TURN_PREFIX, &text),
   866	            ))
   867	        }
   868	        "assistant" => {
   869	            let id = optional_string(value.get("sessionId"))?;
   870	            let text = claude_assistant_text(value)?;
   871	            Some((
   872	                id,
   873	                agent_session_turn_preview(AGENT_SESSION_AGENT_TURN_PREFIX, &text),
   874	            ))
   875	        }
   876	        _ => None,
   877	    }
   878	}

   880	/// What the agent said in words on one transcript line. An assistant record
   881	/// whose content is nothing but `tool_use` blocks said nothing, and yields
   882	/// `None`.
   883	fn claude_assistant_text(value: &Value) -> Option<String> {
   884	    let content = value.get("message")?.get("content")?;
   885	    let text = match content {
   886	        Value::String(text) => text.clone(),
   887	        Value::Array(items) => items
   888	            .iter()
   889	            .filter(|item| optional_string(item.get("type")).as_deref() == Some("text"))
   890	            .filter_map(|item| item.get("text").and_then(Value::as_str))
   891	            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
   892	            .join(" "),
   893	        _ => return None,
   894	    };
   895	
   896	    let text = text.trim();
   897	    (!text.is_empty()).then(|| text.to_string())
   898	}

   900	/// A Claude Code SUBAGENT transcript is stored as its own `.jsonl` and is never
   901	/// resumable — `claude --resume <id>` on one is meaningless — so it must never
   902	/// reach the rail. Two independent discriminators, because each covers what the
   903	/// other cannot: the path is free and also keeps subagents out of the scan's
   904	/// file budget, the content is authoritative and still catches a flat layout.
   905	///
   906	/// Today Claude Code writes them under `<project>/<session>/subagents/`.
   907	fn is_claude_subagent_transcript_path(path: &Path) -> bool {
   908	    path.components()
   909	        .any(|component| component.as_os_str() == "subagents")
   910	}
   911	
   912	/// Every entry of a subagent transcript carries `"isSidechain": true`; every
   913	/// entry of a real session carries `false`. Verified across 2180 transcripts on
   914	/// a live machine: 1177 sidechain files, all of them pure, zero mixed files.
   915	fn is_claude_sidechain_entry(value: &Value) -> bool {
   916	    value.get("isSidechain").and_then(Value::as_bool) == Some(true)
   917	}
   918	
   919	/// Entrypoint values that mean "a program started this run, not the user".
   920	/// Prefixes, so a future `sdk-node` is covered without a code change; adding a
   921	/// new family is a one-line edit here.
   922	const AGENT_LAUNCH_ENTRYPOINT_PREFIXES: &[&str] = &["sdk"];
   923	
   924	/// Helper-agent transcripts — a team lead's dispatched teammates, and any other
   925	/// SDK-driven run — land flat in the same project directory as the user's own
   926	/// sessions, with `isSidechain: false`, `userType: "external"` and no agent name
   927	/// anywhere, so neither discriminator above sees them. What they do carry is how
   928	/// they were launched: every `user`, `assistant` and `attachment` record repeats
   929	/// an `entrypoint`, and a programmatic run is always `sdk-…` (`sdk-cli`,
   930	/// `sdk-py`) where a session the user typed into is `cli` or `claude-vscode`.
   931	///
   932	/// Verified 2026-07-28 across 1073 transcripts on this machine: every one of the
   933	/// 888 dispatched helper runs was `sdk-…`, every human session was `cli` or
   934	/// `claude-vscode`, and no transcript ever mixed the two families. 1072 of the
   935	/// 1073 carry the field within the 256 KB tail this scanner reads.
   936	///
   937	/// This deliberately replaces the "does the first message read like a dispatch
   938	/// prompt?" idea: the user's real sessions often open with pasted logs and
   939	/// instruction-shaped text, and the scanner reads a tail window that usually
   940	/// does not even contain the first message.
   941	fn is_agent_launch_entrypoint(entrypoint: &str) -> bool {
   942	    AGENT_LAUNCH_ENTRYPOINT_PREFIXES
   943	        .iter()
   944	        .any(|prefix| entrypoint.starts_with(prefix))
   945	}
   946	
   947	/// Reads that entrypoint off one transcript line. A line without the field says
   948	/// nothing either way — older transcripts predate it — so it is not evidence of
   949	/// a helper and the transcript is kept.
   950	fn is_claude_agent_launched_entry(value: &Value) -> bool {
   951	    value
   952	        .get("entrypoint")
   953	        .and_then(Value::as_str)
   954	        .is_some_and(is_agent_launch_entrypoint)
   955	}
   956	
   957	/// The same question asked of a file instead of a parsed record, so the scan can
   958	/// skip helper runs before it spends its read budget on them.
   959	///
   960	/// Excluding them at parse time was never enough. A batch of API work can write
   961	/// hundreds of transcripts in an afternoon — 880 of the 1091 here came from one
   962	/// document-extraction job, all in a temporary directory — and the scan reads
   963	/// only the newest 512 files. Sorted by modification time, that batch pushed the
   964	/// user's own sessions out of the scan entirely: 6 of 24 survived. Nothing was
   965	/// wrong with the rule; it just ran too late to matter.
   966	///
   967	/// Reads a bounded head rather than the whole file. Anything unreadable, or
   968	/// whose entrypoint sits past the probe, is kept and settled when the file is
   969	/// parsed in full — the same direction to fail as every other check here.
   970	fn claude_transcript_file_is_agent_launched(path: &Path) -> bool {
   971	    let Ok(head) = read_head_utf8(path, CLAUDE_SESSION_LAUNCH_PROBE_BYTES) else {
   972	        return false;
   973	    };
   974	
   975	    claude_transcript_head_is_agent_launched(&head)
   976	}
   977	
   978	pub fn claude_transcript_head_is_agent_launched(head: &str) -> bool {
   979	    head.lines()
   980	        .filter_map(|line| serde_json::from_str::<Value>(line).ok())
   981	        .any(|value| is_claude_agent_launched_entry(&value))
   982	}

   984	/// Claude Code records its own generated session title on a `type: "ai-title"`
   985	/// line. It is the best title available — it describes the whole session rather
   986	/// than whichever message happened to be last — so it wins outright.
   987	fn claude_ai_title(value: &Value) -> Option<(String, String)> {
   988	    if optional_string(value.get("type"))? != "ai-title" {
   989	        return None;
   990	    }
   991	
   992	    Some((
   993	        optional_string(value.get("sessionId"))?,
   994	        optional_string(value.get("aiTitle"))?,
   995	    ))
   996	}
   997	
   998	/// Openings that mean Claude Code wrote this "user" message, not the user. `<`
   999	/// covers every tagged block it injects (`<command-name>`,
  1000	/// `<local-command-caveat>`); the resume caveat and the interruption notice are
  1001	/// the two it writes as plain sentences.
  1002	///
  1003	/// The interruption matters more than it looks. Pressing Escape in the middle
  1004	/// of an answer is how a session usually ends, so it is disproportionately
  1005	/// likely to be the LAST thing in a transcript — and the row shows the last
  1006	/// thing said. In 617 real user turns sampled on this machine, 50 of them were
  1007	/// exactly "[Request interrupted by user]".
  1008	const CLAUDE_INJECTED_PROMPT_PREFIXES: &[&str] =
  1009	    &["<", "Caveat:", "[Request interrupted"];
  1010	
  1011	/// The first genuine user prompt in the scanned window. Tool results are
  1012	/// `type: "user"` too, so plain `content` text is required and `tool_result`
  1013	/// items are dropped; anything Claude Code wrote for itself is skipped because
  1014	/// none of it says what the session is about.
  1015	fn claude_user_prompt_text(value: &Value) -> Option<(String, String)> {
  1016	    if optional_string(value.get("type"))? != "user" {
  1017	        return None;
  1018	    }
  1019	    if value.get("isMeta").and_then(Value::as_bool) == Some(true) {
  1020	        return None;
  1021	    }
  1022	
  1023	    let id = optional_string(value.get("sessionId"))?;
  1024	    let text = match value.get("message")?.get("content")? {
  1025	        Value::String(text) => text.clone(),
  1026	        Value::Array(items) => items
  1027	            .iter()
  1028	            .filter(|item| optional_string(item.get("type")).as_deref() == Some("text"))
  1029	            .filter_map(|item| item.get("text").and_then(Value::as_str))
  1030	            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
  1031	            .join(" "),
  1032	        _ => return None,
  1033	    };
  1034	
  1035	    let text = text.trim();
  1036	    if text.is_empty()
  1037	        || CLAUDE_INJECTED_PROMPT_PREFIXES
  1038	            .iter()
  1039	            .any(|prefix| text.starts_with(prefix))
  1040	    {
  1041	        return None;
  1042	    }
  1043	
  1044	    Some((id, text.to_string()))
  1045	}

  1047	/// Title preference for a Claude row: the session's own AI title, then whatever
  1048	/// a message yielded, then `<project folder> — <first user prompt>`. The generic
  1049	/// label survives only when nothing else exists — a rail full of "Claude
  1050	/// session" rows tells the user nothing about which session to resume.
  1051	fn claude_display_title(
  1052	    derived: &str,
  1053	    ai_title: Option<&str>,
  1054	    first_prompt: Option<&str>,
  1055	    project_path: Option<&str>,
  1056	) -> String {
  1057	    if let Some(title) = ai_title {
  1058	        return compact_text(title, 80);
  1059	    }
  1060	    if derived != CLAUDE_GENERIC_SESSION_TITLE {
  1061	        return derived.to_string();
  1062	    }
  1063	
  1064	    match (first_prompt, project_path.and_then(path_display_name)) {
  1065	        (Some(prompt), Some(folder)) => compact_text(&format!("{folder} — {prompt}"), 60),
  1066	        (Some(prompt), None) => compact_text(prompt, 60),
  1067	        (None, _) => CLAUDE_GENERIC_SESSION_TITLE.to_string(),
  1068	    }
  1069	}

  1071	fn cmux_resume_commands(agent: &str, id: &str, cwd: Option<&str>) -> Vec<String> {
  1072	    let command = match agent {
  1073	        "codex" => format!("codex resume {id}"),
  1074	        "claude" => format!("claude --resume {id}"),
  1075	        "gemini" => format!("gemini --resume {id}"),
  1076	        "opencode" => format!("opencode --session {id}"),
  1077	        "omp" | "pi" => format!("{agent} --session {id}"),
  1078	        "amp" => format!("amp threads continue {id}"),
  1079	        "antigravity" | "agy" => format!("agy --conversation {id}"),
  1080	        "rovo" | "acli" => format!("acli rovodev run --restore {id}"),
  1081	        "cursor" | "cursor-agent" => format!("cursor-agent --resume {id}"),
  1082	        other => format!("{other} --resume {id}"),
  1083	    };
  1084	
  1085	    match cwd.filter(|value| !value.trim().is_empty()) {
  1086	        Some(cwd) => vec![
  1087	            command.clone(),
  1088	            format!("cd {} && {command}", shell_quote(cwd)),
  1089	        ],
  1090	        None => vec![command],
  1091	    }
  1092	}

  1094	fn merge_codex_record(existing: &mut AgentSessionRecord, candidate: AgentSessionRecord) {
  1095	    let previous_title = existing.title.clone();
  1096	    let candidate_title = candidate.title.clone();
  1097	    merge_agent_session_record(existing, candidate);
  1098	    existing.title = better_codex_title(previous_title, candidate_title);
  1099	}
  1100	
  1101	fn merge_agent_session_record(existing: &mut AgentSessionRecord, candidate: AgentSessionRecord) {
  1102	    if existing.description.is_none() {
  1103	        existing.description = candidate.description.clone();
  1104	    }
  1105	
  1106	    if existing.model.is_none() {
  1107	        existing.model = candidate.model.clone();
  1108	    }
  1109	
  1110	    if existing.project_path.is_none() {
  1111	        existing.project_path = candidate.project_path.clone();
  1112	    }
  1113	
  1114	    // The fuller read wins, whichever record it came from. One session can be
  1115	    // described by more than one file, and each count is a floor — the bigger
  1116	    // floor is the one closer to the truth. (`None` sorts below every `Some`,
  1117	    // so a record that counted nothing never overwrites one that did.)
  1118	    existing.message_count = existing.message_count.max(candidate.message_count);
  1119	
  1120	    if existing.latest_turn_preview.is_none() {
  1121	        existing.latest_turn_preview = candidate.latest_turn_preview.clone();
  1122	    }
  1123	
  1124	    let candidate_is_newer = candidate
  1125	        .last_activity
  1126	        .as_ref()
  1127	        .is_some_and(|candidate_activity| {
  1128	            existing
  1129	                .last_activity
  1130	                .as_ref()
  1131	                .map_or(true, |existing_activity| {
  1132	                    candidate_activity > existing_activity
  1133	                })
  1134	        });
  1135	
  1136	    if candidate_is_newer {
  1137	        existing.title = candidate.title;
  1138	        existing.description = candidate.description.or(existing.description.take());
  1139	        existing.model = candidate.model.or(existing.model.take());
  1140	        existing.project_path = candidate.project_path.or(existing.project_path.take());
  1141	        existing.last_activity = candidate.last_activity;
  1142	        existing.latest_turn_preview = candidate
  1143	            .latest_turn_preview
  1144	            .or(existing.latest_turn_preview.take());
  1145	    }
  1146	
  1147	    for command in candidate.resume_commands {
  1148	        if !existing.resume_commands.contains(&command) {
  1149	            existing.resume_commands.push(command);
  1150	        }
  1151	    }
  1152	}

  1207	fn agent_display_label(agent: &str) -> String {
  1208	    match agent {
  1209	        "codex" => "Codex".to_string(),
  1210	        "claude" => "Claude".to_string(),
  1211	        "gemini" => "Gemini".to_string(),
  1212	        "opencode" => "OpenCode".to_string(),
  1213	        "cursor" | "cursor-agent" => "Cursor".to_string(),
  1214	        "antigravity" | "agy" => "Antigravity".to_string(),
  1215	        "rovo" | "acli" => "Rovo".to_string(),
  1216	        other => {
  1217	            let mut chars = other.chars();
  1218	            match chars.next() {
  1219	                Some(first) => first.to_uppercase().chain(chars).collect(),
  1220	                None => "Agent".to_string(),
  1221	            }
  1222	        }
  1223	    }
  1224	}
  1225	
  1226	fn compact_text(value: &str, max_chars: usize) -> String {
  1227	    let trimmed = value.split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" ");
  1228	    if trimmed.chars().count() <= max_chars {
  1229	        return trimmed;
  1230	    }
  1231	
  1232	    let mut compacted = trimmed
  1233	        .chars()
  1234	        .take(max_chars.saturating_sub(1))
  1235	        .collect::<String>();
  1236	    compacted.push('…');
  1237	    compacted
  1238	}

  1244	        .map(str::trim)
  1245	        .filter(|value| !value.is_empty())
  1246	        .map(ToOwned::to_owned)
  1247	}

  1286	fn branch_hint_from_text(text: &str) -> Option<String> {
  1287	    let lower_text = text.to_ascii_lowercase();
  1288	    for marker in ["branch:", "branch=", "branch "] {
  1289	        let mut search_start = 0;
  1290	        while let Some(offset) = lower_text[search_start..].find(marker) {
  1291	            let index = search_start + offset;
  1292	            if index > 0 {
  1293	                let previous = lower_text.as_bytes()[index - 1] as char;
  1294	                if previous.is_ascii_alphanumeric() {
  1295	                    search_start = index + marker.len();
  1296	                    continue;
  1297	                }
  1298	            }
  1299	
  1300	            let suffix = &text[index + marker.len()..];
  1301	            if let Some(branch) = git_ref_token_from_text(suffix) {
  1302	                return Some(branch);
  1303	            }
  1304	            search_start = index + marker.len();
  1305	        }
  1306	    }
  1307	
  1308	    None
  1309	}
  1310	
  1311	fn git_ref_token_from_text(text: &str) -> Option<String> {
  1312	    let token: String = text
  1313	        .trim_start_matches(|character: char| {
  1314	            character.is_whitespace() || matches!(character, '`' | '"' | '\'')
  1315	        })
  1316	        .chars()
  1317	        .take_while(|character| {
  1318	            character.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(character, '.' | '_' | '-' | '/')
  1319	        })
  1320	        .collect();
  1321	    if token.is_empty()
  1322	        || token
  1323	            .chars()
  1324	            .all(|character| matches!(character, '.' | '_' | '-' | '/'))
  1325	    {
  1326	        return None;
  1327	    }
  1328	
  1329	    Some(token)
  1330	}
  1331	
  1332	fn task_id_from_text(text: &str) -> Option<String> {
  1333	    let lower_text = text.to_ascii_lowercase();
  1334	    for (index, _) in lower_text.match_indices("tsk") {
  1335	        if index > 0 {
  1336	            let previous = lower_text.as_bytes()[index - 1] as char;
  1337	            if previous.is_ascii_alphanumeric() {
  1338	                continue;
  1339	            }
  1340	        }
  1341	
  1342	        let suffix =
  1343	            lower_text[index + 3..].trim_start_matches(['-', '_', '/', '#', '[', ' ', ':']);
  1344	        let digits: String = suffix
  1345	            .chars()
  1346	            .take_while(|character| character.is_ascii_digit())
  1347	            .collect();
  1348	        if !digits.is_empty() {
  1349	            return Some(format!("TSK-{digits}"));
  1350	        }
  1351	    }
  1352	
  1353	    None
  1354	}

  1356	fn pull_request_hint_from_text(text: &str) -> Option<String> {
  1357	    pull_request_number_after_marker(text, "pull request")
  1358	        .or_else(|| pull_request_number_after_marker(text, "pr"))
  1359	        .or_else(|| {
  1360	            link_hint_from_text(text)
  1361	                .as_deref()
  1362	                .and_then(github_pull_request_number_from_url)
  1363	        })
  1364	        .map(|number| format!("PR #{number}"))
  1365	}

  1367	fn pull_request_number_after_marker(text: &str, marker: &str) -> Option<String> {
  1368	    let lower_text = text.to_ascii_lowercase();
  1369	    let mut search_start = 0;
  1370	    while let Some(offset) = lower_text[search_start..].find(marker) {
  1371	        let index = search_start + offset;
  1372	        if index > 0 {
  1373	            let previous = lower_text.as_bytes()[index - 1] as char;
  1374	            if previous.is_ascii_alphanumeric() {
  1375	                search_start = index + marker.len();
  1376	                continue;
  1377	            }
  1378	        }
  1379	
  1380	        let suffix = &text[index + marker.len()..];
  1381	        let suffix = suffix.trim_start_matches([' ', '#', '-', ':']);
  1382	        let digits: String = suffix
  1383	            .chars()
  1384	            .take_while(|character| character.is_ascii_digit())
  1385	            .collect();
  1386	        if !digits.is_empty() {
  1387	            return Some(digits);
  1388	        }
  1389	
  1390	        search_start = index + marker.len();
  1391	    }
  1392	
  1393	    None
  1394	}

  1396	fn link_hint_from_text(text: &str) -> Option<String> {
  1397	    for scheme in ["https://", "http://"] {
  1398	        let mut search_start = 0;
  1399	        while let Some(offset) = text[search_start..].find(scheme) {
  1400	            let index = search_start + offset;
  1401	            let suffix = &text[index..];
  1402	            let end = suffix
  1403	                .char_indices()
  1404	                .find_map(|(index, character)| character.is_whitespace().then_some(index))
  1405	                .unwrap_or(suffix.len());
  1406	            let link = suffix[..end].trim_end_matches(['.', ',', ';', ':', ')', ']', '}', '"']);
  1407	            if !link.is_empty() {
  1408	                return Some(link.to_string());
  1409	            }
  1410	
  1411	            search_start = index + scheme.len();
  1412	        }
  1413	    }
  1414	
  1415	    None
  1416	}

  1418	fn github_pull_request_number_from_url(url: &str) -> Option<String> {

  1420	        return None;

  1422	
  1423	    let lower_url = url.to_ascii_lowercase();
  1424	    let index = lower_url.find("/pull/")? + "/pull/".len();
  1425	    let digits: String = url[index..]
  1426	        .chars()
  1427	        .take_while(|character| character.is_ascii_digit())

  1440	fn timestampish_string(value: Option<&Value>) -> Option<String> {
  1441	    let value = value?;
  1442	    match value {
  1443	        Value::String(value) => {
  1444	            let trimmed = value.trim();
  1445	            if trimmed.is_empty() {
  1446	                None
  1447	            } else if let Ok(number) = trimmed.parse::<f64>() {
  1448	                unix_timestamp_number_to_iso(number).or_else(|| Some(trimmed.to_string()))
  1449	            } else {
  1450	                Some(trimmed.to_string())
  1451	            }
  1452	        }
  1453	        Value::Number(number) => number.as_f64().and_then(unix_timestamp_number_to_iso),
  1454	        _ => None,
  1455	    }
  1456	}
  1457	
  1458	fn unix_timestamp_number_to_iso(value: f64) -> Option<String> {
  1459	    if !value.is_finite() || value < 0.0 {
  1460	        return None;
  1461	    }
  1462	
  1463	    let seconds_value = if value >= 1_000_000_000_000.0 {
  1464	        value / 1000.0
  1465	    } else {
  1466	        value
  1467	    };
  1468	    let mut seconds = seconds_value.floor() as i64;
  1469	    let mut millis = ((seconds_value - seconds as f64) * 1000.0).floor() as u32;
  1470	    if millis >= 1000 {
  1471	        seconds += 1;
  1472	        millis = 0;
  1473	    }
  1474	    Some(unix_seconds_to_iso8601(seconds, millis))
  1475	}
  1476	
  1477	fn unix_seconds_to_iso8601(seconds: i64, millis: u32) -> String {
  1478	    let days = seconds.div_euclid(86_400);
  1479	    let seconds_of_day = seconds.rem_euclid(86_400);
  1480	    let (year, month, day) = civil_from_days(days);
  1481	    let hour = seconds_of_day / 3600;
  1482	    let minute = (seconds_of_day % 3600) / 60;
  1483	    let second = seconds_of_day % 60;
  1484	
  1485	    if millis > 0 {
  1486	        format!("{year:04}-{month:02}-{day:02}T{hour:02}:{minute:02}:{second:02}.{millis:03}Z")
  1487	    } else {
  1488	        format!("{year:04}-{month:02}-{day:02}T{hour:02}:{minute:02}:{second:02}Z")
  1489	    }
  1490	}
  1491	
  1492	fn civil_from_days(days: i64) -> (i64, u32, u32) {
  1493	    let days = days + 719_468;
  1494	    let era = if days >= 0 { days } else { days - 146_096 } / 146_097;
  1495	    let day_of_era = days - era * 146_097;
  1496	    let year_of_era =
  1497	        (day_of_era - day_of_era / 1460 + day_of_era / 36_524 - day_of_era / 146_096) / 365;
  1498	    let year = year_of_era + era * 400;
  1499	    let day_of_year = day_of_era - (365 * year_of_era + year_of_era / 4 - year_of_era / 100);
  1500	    let month_prime = (5 * day_of_year + 2) / 153;
  1501	    let day = day_of_year - (153 * month_prime + 2) / 5 + 1;
  1502	    let month = month_prime + if month_prime < 10 { 3 } else { -9 };
  1503	    let year = year + if month <= 2 { 1 } else { 0 };
  1504	
  1505	    (year, month as u32, day as u32)
  1506	}

  1508	fn title_from_claude_message(value: &Value) -> Option<String> {
  1509	    let content = value
  1510	        .get("message")
  1511	        .and_then(|message| message.get("content"))
  1512	        .and_then(value_to_text)
  1513	        .or_else(|| value.get("summary").and_then(value_to_text))?;
  1514	
  1515	    let trimmed = content.trim();
  1516	    if trimmed.is_empty() {
  1517	        return None;
  1518	    }
  1519	
  1520	    Some(trimmed.chars().take(80).collect())
  1521	}
  1522	
  1523	fn value_to_text(value: &Value) -> Option<String> {
  1524	    match value {
  1525	        Value::String(value) => Some(value.clone()),
  1526	        Value::Array(values) => values
  1527	            .iter()
  1528	            .filter_map(|item| {
  1529	                item.get("text")
  1530	                    .and_then(Value::as_str)
  1531	                    .or_else(|| item.get("content").and_then(Value::as_str))
  1532	            })
  1533	            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
  1534	            .join(" ")
  1535	            .into(),
  1536	        _ => None,
  1537	    }
  1538	}

  1540	fn jsonl_files(root: &Path) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
  1541	    let mut files = Vec::new();
  1542	    let Ok(entries) = fs::read_dir(root) else {
  1543	        return files;
  1544	    };
  1545	
  1546	    for entry in entries.flatten() {
  1547	        let path = entry.path();
  1548	        if path.is_dir() {
  1549	            files.extend(jsonl_files(&path));
  1550	        } else if path.extension().and_then(|ext| ext.to_str()) == Some("jsonl") {
  1551	            files.push(path);
  1552	        }
  1553	    }
  1554	
  1555	    files
  1556	}

  1558	fn cmux_hook_session_files(root: &Path) -> Vec<(String, PathBuf)> {
  1559	    let mut files = Vec::new();
  1560	    let Ok(entries) = fs::read_dir(root) else {
  1561	        return files;
  1562	    };
  1563	
  1564	    for entry in entries.flatten() {
  1565	        let path = entry.path();
  1566	        if !path.is_file() {
  1567	            continue;
  1568	        }
  1569	
  1570	        let Some(name) = path.file_name().and_then(|name| name.to_str()) else {
  1571	            continue;
  1572	        };
  1573	        let Some(agent) = name.strip_suffix("-hook-sessions.json") else {
  1574	            continue;
  1575	        };
  1576	        if agent.is_empty() {
  1577	            continue;
  1578	        }
  1579	
  1580	        files.push((agent.to_string(), path));
  1581	    }
  1582	
  1583	    files
  1584	}

  1586	pub fn read_tail_utf8(path: &Path, max_bytes: usize) -> std::io::Result<String> {
  1587	    let mut file = fs::File::open(path)?;
  1588	    let len = file.metadata()?.len();
  1589	    let start = len.saturating_sub(max_bytes as u64);
  1590	    file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(start))?;
  1591	
  1592	    let mut bytes = Vec::new();
  1593	    file.read_to_end(&mut bytes)?;
  1594	    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes);
  1595	    if start == 0 {
  1596	        return Ok(text.into_owned());
  1597	    }
  1598	
  1599	    Ok(text
  1600	        .split_once('\n')
  1601	        .map(|(_, tail)| tail.to_string())
  1602	        .unwrap_or_default())
  1603	}
  1604	
  1605	pub fn read_head_utf8(path: &Path, max_bytes: usize) -> std::io::Result<String> {
  1606	    let file = fs::File::open(path)?;
  1607	    let mut bytes = Vec::new();
  1608	    file.take(max_bytes as u64).read_to_end(&mut bytes)?;
  1609	
  1610	    Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes).into_owned())
  1611	}
  1612	
  1613	/// A window from the start of the file and a window from the end, joined.
  1614	///
  1615	/// A file that fits inside the two windows put together is read WHOLE instead,
  1616	/// decided on its real length. The obvious-looking alternative — stitch the two
  1617	/// windows and notice afterwards that the head already ended with the tail —
  1618	/// only recognises a file that fits inside ONE window. Anything between one
  1619	/// window and two got the middle of the file handed to the caller twice, and
  1620	/// the caller counts what it is given.
  1621	fn read_head_and_tail_utf8(
  1622	    path: &Path,
  1623	    head_bytes: usize,
  1624	    tail_bytes: usize,
  1625	) -> std::io::Result<String> {
  1626	    let combined = head_bytes.saturating_add(tail_bytes);
  1627	    if fs::metadata(path)?.len() <= combined as u64 {
  1628	        return read_head_utf8(path, combined);
  1629	    }
  1630	
  1631	    let head = read_head_utf8(path, head_bytes)?;
  1632	    let tail = read_tail_utf8(path, tail_bytes)?;
  1633	    if tail.is_empty() {
  1634	        return Ok(head);
  1635	    }
  1636	
  1637	    Ok(format!("{}\n{}", head.trim_end_matches('\n'), tail))
  1638	}
  1639	
  1640	fn modified_time(path: &Path) -> Option<std::time::SystemTime> {
  1641	    fs::metadata(path)
  1642	        .and_then(|metadata| metadata.modified())
  1643	        .ok()
  1644	}

  1646	pub fn decode_claude_project_dir(name: &str) -> Option<String> {

  1649	
  1650	pub fn decode_claude_project_dir_with_users_root(name: &str, users_root: &Path) -> Option<String> {
  1651	    let rest = name.strip_prefix("-Users-")?;
  1652	    let segments: Vec<&str> = rest
  1653	        .split('-')
  1654	        .filter(|segment| !segment.is_empty())
  1655	        .collect();
  1656	    if segments.is_empty() {
  1657	        return None;
  1658	    }
  1659	
  1660	    let mut path = users_root.to_path_buf();
  1661	    let mut index = 0;
  1662	    while index < segments.len() {
  1663	        let mut chosen_len = 1;
  1664	        for len in (1..=(segments.len() - index)).rev() {
  1665	            let candidate = segments[index..index + len].join("-");
  1666	            if path.join(&candidate).exists() {
  1667	                chosen_len = len;
  1668	                break;
  1669	            }
  1670	        }
  1671	
  1672	        path.push(segments[index..index + chosen_len].join("-"));
  1673	        index += chosen_len;
  1674	    }
  1675	
  1676	    Some(path.display().to_string())
  1677	}

  1679	fn shell_quote(value: &str) -> String {
  1680	    if value.is_empty() {
  1681	        return "''".to_string();
  1682	    }
  1683	    format!("'{}'", value.replace('\'', "'\\''"))
  1684	}

  1709	    /// A Claude session with an actual back-and-forth in it, and the tool
  1710	    /// traffic that ran in between: two things the user typed (one of them a
  1711	    /// slash command, which is not conversation), two answers in words, one
  1712	    /// tool call and one tool result.

  1714	    /// The same fixture is written out line for line in
  1715	    /// `tauri-svelte-preview/scripts/localSourceFs.test.mjs`. Both scanners
  1716	    /// fill the same rail, so a row has to read the same whichever one produced
  1717	    /// it.
  1718	    const CONVERSATION_JSONL: &str = concat!(
  1719	        r#"{"type":"user","isSidechain":false,"sessionId":"S9","cwd":"/Users/dev/work/mac-command-bar","timestamp":"2026-07-29T09:00:00Z","message":{"role":"user","content":"Fix the resume rail"}}"#,
  1720	        "\n",
  1721	        r#"{"type":"assistant","isSidechain":false,"sessionId":"S9","timestamp":"2026-07-29T09:01:00Z","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Reading the scanner now."}]}}"#,
  1722	        "\n",
  1723	        r#"{"type":"assistant","isSidechain":false,"sessionId":"S9","timestamp":"2026-07-29T09:02:00Z","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"t1","name":"Read","input":{}}]}}"#,
  1724	        "\n",
  1725	        r#"{"type":"user","isSidechain":false,"sessionId":"S9","timestamp":"2026-07-29T09:03:00Z","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"tool_result","content":"File does not exist."}]}}"#,
  1726	        "\n",
  1727	        r#"{"type":"user","isSidechain":false,"sessionId":"S9","timestamp":"2026-07-29T09:04:00Z","message":{"role":"user","content":"<command-name>compact</command-name>"}}"#,
  1728	        "\n",
  1729	        r#"{"type":"assistant","isSidechain":false,"sessionId":"S9","timestamp":"2026-07-29T09:05:00Z","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The  rail was\n  reading the wrong file."}]}}"#,
  1730	    );
  1731	
  1732	    /// The same session ending on an answer far longer than one line, so the
  1733	    /// cut is pinned. Also mirrored in the TypeScript suite.
  1734	    const LONG_ANSWER_TEXT: &str = "The scanner was reading the wrong file the whole time, which is why every row said Claude session and none of them said anything else at all";
  1735	
  1736	    /// A Codex session with the agent's reply in it, on top of the opening

  1739	        r#"{"timestamp":"2026-07-28T16:42:17.000Z","type":"session_meta","payload":{"id":"019fa964","cwd":"/Users/dev/work/rental-management","originator":"codex-tui","thread_source":"user","source":"cli"}}"#,
  1740	        "\n",
  1741	        r##"{"timestamp":"2026-07-28T16:42:18.000Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"# AGENTS.md instructions for /Users/dev/work/rental-management"}]}}"##,

  1744	        "\n",

  1754	    fn claude_rows_carry_how_many_turns_were_said_and_the_last_of_them() {

  1834	    /// Pressing Escape in the middle of an answer is how a session usually
  1835	    /// ends, and Claude writes that as a user message reading "[Request
  1836	    /// interrupted by user]". It is not something the user said, so it is not a
  1837	    /// turn — and because the row shows the LAST turn, letting it through put
  1838	    /// "You: [Request interrupted by user]" on the most prominent line of the
  1839	    /// card, where it says nothing at all about the session. The row falls back
  1840	    /// to the last thing that really was said.

  1842	    fn an_interrupted_request_is_neither_counted_nor_shown() {

  1847	        let records = parse_claude_jsonl(&interrupted, "/Users/dev/work/mac-command-bar");
